grammar_tip: 'Apfel' is masculine. In the accusative case (direct object), 'ein' becomes 'einen'.
'Salat' is masculine. After the verb 'kaufen' (requires accusative), we use 'einen'.
'Kaffee' is masculine. The accusative form of 'ein' is 'einen'.
'Tomate' is feminine. The accusative form is exactly the same as the nominative: 'eine'.

'Ei' is neutral. The accusative form is exactly the same as the nominative: 'ein'.
'Brot' is neutral. The article 'ein' remains 'ein' in the accusative case.
'Apfel' is masculine. The definite article changes from 'der' to 'den' in the accusative case.
'Joghurt' is masculine. The direct object takes the accusative 'den'.

meaning: I am not hungry (I have no hunger).
grammar_tip: 'Hunger' is masculine. Negating it in the accusative case requires 'keinen'.
'Schinken' is masculine. The direct object negation is 'keinen'.
'Marmelade' is feminine. Negating it in the accusative case is 'keine'.
'Milch' is feminine. The negative article is 'keine'.
'Bier' is neutral. Negating it in the accusative case is 'kein'.
'Fleisch' is neutral. The negative article is 'kein'.
'Eier' is plural. Plural nouns are negated with 'keine'.
'Tomaten' is plural. The plural negative article is 'keine'.
Uncountable liquids like 'Wasser' take the Nullartikel (no article) when speaking generally.
Uncountable materials and foods like 'Fleisch' take the Nullartikel.
Plural nouns without a specific quantity or definite 'the' take the Nullartikel (they have no indefinite 'a/an').
